newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade union congress attacks capitalism.
newsitem.headline: German trade union congress attacks capitalism.

text.p: The German Federation of Trade Unions on Wednesday launched a congress intended to agree a new "basic programme" of goals with an attack on what it called the growth of "unfettered" capitalism in Germany.
Dieter Schulte, chairman of the DBG union federation, said workers should beware of employers and politicians who were increasingly putting profits before the overall good of society.
"I don't want an unfettered market economy and an authoritarian, anti-social republic," Schulte said in the text of a speech released before delivery.

Schulte said Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government had "deregulated, privatised and scaled down" social costs over the last 14 years at the expense of rising unemployment and increasing social injustice.

Schulte said the DGB still saw full employment in Germany as an achievable goal and berated Kohl for his recent admission that a previous target of halving current jobless levels by the year 2000 could have been over-optimistic.
Despite the criticisms voiced on Wednesday, one of the key changes contained in a draft of the federation's new programme is a qualified acceptance of the role of the market economy.

The initial draft, which is to be debated over the next three days, says in a contraversial phrase that a "socially-oriented market economy" is "better-suited than other economic models to the goals of trade unions".
Nearly 600 motions are due to heard proposing changes to the 34-page draft programme, drawn up in 1981 and based on the traditional view of the conflict between capital and labour.
Some union delegates are seeking to postpone the drawing up of a new programme altogether.
